design_intent.original_text: Make it a 3x3x3 cube with no gravity: players still alternate placing X and O in any empty cell; any straight line of three cells through the cube (rows, columns, pillars and every diagonal, 49 lines in total) wins; a full cube with no line is a draw.
preserve: Players alternate turns placing X and O.
A move places a mark in an empty cell.
changes: A straight line of three cells through the cube wins, including rows, columns, pillars, and every diagonal; there are 49 winning lines in total.
A full cube with no winning line is a draw.
constraints: No gravity: a player may place a mark in any empty cell.

lift_plan.source_xy_policy: Keep the bounded x and y axes at extent 3, the empty/X/O cell values, X-first alternating turns, and the rule that a placement requires an empty cell. Do not add gravity or change restart and quit behavior.
lift_plan.neighborhood: Straight lines use bounded steps along x, y, and z, including face and space diagonals. The 3×3×3 cube has 49 winning lines of three cells: 27 axis-aligned lines, 18 face diagonals, and 4 space diagonals. Lines do not wrap.
lift_plan.movement: On a turn, the current player places their mark at any empty (x,y,z) cell. An occupied cell or a placement after a terminal outcome is rejected without changing state. A legal nonterminal placement passes the turn to the other player.
lift_plan.outcomes: A player wins when their placement completes any straight line of three cells in the cube. Check for a win before a draw. If all 27 cells are occupied and no winning line exists, the result is a draw.
lift_plan.presentation: Show the board as the engine-owned continuous cube volume, with X and O at their 3D cell positions. Retain turn, win, and draw status information; do not split the cube into layer panels.
lift_plan.input: Clicking a cell supplies its full (x,y,z) coordinate. The engine-provided '[' and ']' keys and on-screen buttons select a depth layer for picking inner cells. Retain the source restart and quit inputs.
z_equals_one_tests: With z at extent 1, the board has the same nine cells and eight winning lines as the Source 3×3 board.
With z at extent 1, legal placements, alternating turns, wins, draws, and rejected placements must match the Source.

z_gt_one_tests.name: Diagonal within a depth layer wins
Any empty depth cell is playable without support

source_game_spec.summary: Two players alternate placing X and O on a 3×3 grid; three in a row wins, and a full board without a win is a draw.

initial_setup.description: Every cell is empty; X moves first, with no winner or draw.

actions.legal_when: There is no winner or draw, x and y are each within 0 through 2, and board[y][x] is empty.
actions.effect: Set board[y][x] to the current player's value. Check for a win, then a draw; only if neither occurs, switch the current player from 1 to 2 or from 2 to 1. An illegal placement returns false without changing state.

actions.legal_when: An R keydown is received; the source imposes no game-state restriction.
actions.effect: Reset the board, current player, winner, and draw state to their initial values.

actions.legal_when: Escape is pressed or a window-close event is received.
actions.effect: Stop the application loop; no game outcome is assigned.

outcomes.condition: After a placement, any row, column, or either diagonal has all three cells equal to the current player's value.
After a placement, no winning line exists and every board cell is nonzero.

controls.control: Left-button down; convert pointer position to a cell using the board's left and top offsets and cell size.

presentation.description: A Pygame window displays a status line showing the turn, winner, or draw; instructions; and a 3×3 board of rounded cells with blue X marks and orange O marks. The display loop is capped at 60 frames per second.
